full_text_en:
OBE-Factory Omahet & Baumgartner Co., Ltd. v. Zhejiang Kanghua Glasses Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Infringement of Invention Patent

【Ruling Summary】

1. Where a method patent claim does not explicitly define the sequence of steps, it shall be determined whether the steps should be carried out in a specific order by reference to the specification and drawings, the patent prosecution history, the overall technical solution recorded in the claim, and the logical relationship between the steps.

2. When determining the scope of protection of a patent claim, the patent specification and drawings, other claims in the patent claim set, and the patent prosecution history may be used to interpret the claim.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Shen Zi No. 980

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): OBE-Factory Omahet & Baumgartner Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Ispringen, Federal Republic of Germany.

Legal Representatives: Eric Schaefer, Ulrich Rumelin, Chief Executive Officers.

Authorized Agents: Dong Wei, Attorney at Beijing P. H. Law Firm.

Authorized Agent: Gu Shan, female, Patent Agent at Beijing P. H. Law Firm, residing at Room 501, Door 3, Building 5, Yongtai Yuan, Haidian District, Beijing.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Zhejiang Kanghua Glasses Co., Ltd., domiciled at: No. 208, Xinggang Road, Chenyu Town, Yuhuan County, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Gao Kehu, Chairman of the Board.

Authorized Agents: Liu Ping, Attorney at Beijing Dejun Law Firm.

Authorized Agent: Li Zhong, Attorney at Beijing Dejun Law Firm.

In the case concerning a dispute over infringement of an invention patent between the applicant for retrial, OBE-Factory Omahet & Baumgartner Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as OBE), and the respondent, Zhejiang Kanghua Glasses Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kanghua), the Beijing High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2006) Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 1367 (hereinafter referred to as the second-instance judgment) on December 20, 2006, which has already become legally effective. In September 2008, OBE applied to this Court for a retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review this case, and the review has now been concluded.

OBE applied for a retrial on the following grounds: 1. The core issue in this case is whether the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent in suit. On this issue, the second-instance judgment erred in finding facts and applying the law. 2. The second-instance judgment lacked legal basis when it incorporated two new technical features from the patent specification into claim 1, namely, "the hinge member not being separated from the metal strip" and "the steps being performed in a fixed sequential order," which are not recorded in claim 1. 3. The technical problem addressed by the patent in suit is that the prior art used profile materials to produce spring hinges, requiring complex processing techniques, low yield rates, and high manufacturing costs. The patent in suit could substitute inexpensive strip materials for profile materials and use non-cutting (stamping) methods instead of complex cutting methods. Claim 1 does not limit the steps to include assembling the spring hinge. The description on page 1, lines 29-31 of the patent specification describes the assembly steps of the spring hinge, which are irrelevant to the scope of protection of claim 1 and cannot be used for further limitation or interpretation of claim 1, and cannot be used to incorporate the technical feature of "the hinge member not being separated from the metal strip" into claim 1. 4. The incidental technical problem of "the spring parts being supplied in bulk, thus requiring troublesome alignment before assembly at the correct positions" is solved by the preferred embodiment of "the hinge member not being separated from the metal strip." The technical feature in claim 3, "installing the spring part on the hinge member while the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip," indicates that the technical solution of claim 1 does not require separating the hinge member from the metal strip after completing the steps described in claim 1. The "non-separation of the hinge member from the metal strip" is merely a technical feature achieving an additional purpose, recorded in claim 3, and is not an essential technical feature of claim 1. 5. Claim 1 merely describes the steps of the patented method, without limiting the order of the steps. The key to solving the technical problem is the steps themselves in claim 1, not the order of the steps. The two embodiments in the specification adopt steps in different orders, also indicating that the steps in claim 1 can be performed in different orders. The scope of protection of claim 1 covers various combinations of orders of said steps. The second-instance judgment's finding that "the steps in claim 1 are performed in a fixed sequential order and cannot be changed" contradicts the description in the specification and constitutes a factual error. OBE requested this Court to set aside the second-instance judgment, dismiss the respondent's appeal, and affirm the judgment of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court (2002) Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 5048.

Kanghua argued in defense: 1. The relationship between the steps in claim 1 is a sequentially ordered, fixed progressive relationship, premised on maintaining the connection between the hinge member and the metal strip. Discarding the limitation regarding the relationship between steps and the premise would directly lead to the inability to achieve the task of the patent in suit and the two technical effects of eliminating the handling step and avoiding manual alignment. 2. The accused method does not have the two essential technical features of the patent in suit: "connection between the hinge member and the metal strip" and the fixed order of steps, thus does not constitute infringement. 3. The differences between the accused method and claim 1 are: the patent in suit uses metal "strip," while the accused method uses self-cut metal "bar" of limited length; step two of the patent in suit uses "cutting," while the accused method uses "stamping," which are completely different processing means with different results; in forming the shoulder, the patent in suit uses "stamping," while the accused method uses "die forging," which are different processing techniques, and the patent in suit completes it in one operation, while the accused method requires manual and mechanical combination and repeated operations. 4. The patented method did not fully express the "relationship and condition between steps," and the technical feature in claim 1, "cutting out an area substantially matching the shape of the hinge member," is ambiguous in meaning. The scope of protection of claim 1 should be interpreted in light of the specification and drawings. 5. During the substantive examination of the patent in suit, OBE expressly undertook the limitation of claim 1, namely, "when the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip and thus positioned at a predetermined location, stamping or deforming the hinge member can already improve the method of assembling spring hinge parts." By ignoring this undertaking and expanding the scope of protection of the claim in the infringement lawsuit, OBE engaged in an act of estoppel, which should be prohibited by law.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the first-instance court) found the following facts upon trial: On April 24, 1996, OBE filed an invention patent application with the State Intellectual Property Office of the People's Republic of China, with application number 96191123.9, titled "Method for Manufacturing Spring Hinges." The patent was granted on October 24, 2001. The granted claim 1 reads: "1. A method for manufacturing a spring hinge, the hinge comprising at least one housing, one hinge member, and one spring, characterized in that the method comprises the following steps: providing a metal strip for forming the hinge member; cutting out an area substantially matching the shape of the hinge member; forming a circular part by stamping to form a shoulder of the hinge member; punching out a hinge hole of the hinge member."

On June 24, 2002, OBE filed a lawsuit with the first-instance court, alleging that Kanghua, without OBE's permission, manufactured, used, offered for sale, and sold spring hinge products falling within the scope of protection of the patent in suit for business purposes, constituting patent infringement. OBE also claimed that Kanghua had been manufacturing, selling, offering for sale, and using spring hinge products across the country in recent years, causing serious harm to the patent in suit and inflicting substantial economic losses on OBE. OBE requested the first-instance court to order Kanghua: 1. to cease the infringing acts; 2. to publicly apologize; 3. to destroy the molds and tools used for manufacturing the infringing products; 4. to compensate for economic losses (including royalties for the period of provisional protection) of RMB 4.15 million; 5. to bear OBE's reasonable expenses (including attorney fees, travel expenses, investigation and evidence collection fees); 6. to bear the litigation costs of this case.

In the specification of the patent in suit, the following is recorded: "As is well known, a spring hinge has a housing for installing a spring part, which can move with the spring hinge connected to the temple of the glasses beyond the normal wearing position, and applies a pre-stress to the temple, pressing the temple against the wearer's head. It has been proven that the disadvantage of such spring hinges is high manufacturing costs." "This spring part generally consists of a hinge member, a locking member, and a spring part. Due to the very small sizes of these parts, assembly is quite complicated. Moreover, since these parts are usually supplied in bulk, troublesome alignment is first required to assemble each part at the correct position. Therefore, the task of the present invention is to provide an economical method for manufacturing spring hinges and to improve the handling of parts, thereby producing good economic benefits." "In the present invention, the hinge member processed from metal strip is installed with the spring part and preferably the locking member while the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip, thus on the one hand eliminating the intermediate cushioning of the hinge member before assembly, and on the other hand eliminating the alignment of the hinge member." "The assembled parts are not cut off from the metal strip, thus making handling for use in the spring hinge housing particularly convenient."

On August 10, 2005, the first-instance court went to Kanghua's location and inspected the processing and production process of the products in dispute. Through inspection, Kanghua's processing process was as follows: 1. manually feeding the metal strip into a punch press to punch out the hinge member; 2. manually clamping the front part of the hinge member with pliers and using a forging press to round the rear part of the hinge member; 3. manually clamping the front part of the hinge member with pliers and inserting the hinge member into a hole-punching machine to punch a hole; 4. manually threading a wire through the front circular hole of the hinge member, stringing several hinge members together, and then polishing them using a polishing wheel. The first-instance court recorded the above process with a DV and produced a disc, which was served to both parties for cross-examination. OBE believed that Kanghua's processing process was precisely the method protected by claim 1 of the patent in suit. Kanghua argued: 1. The patented method is a four-step sequential spring hinge manufacturing method, while Kanghua's processing process consists of three processing units with adjustable order, lacking the feature of sequential progression. 2. The second step of the patented method is cutting, and the cut area does not separate from the metal strip, while Kanghua's process is "blanking," thus the methods are different and the results are different. 3. The third step of the patented method is "stamping to form a circular part," while Kanghua uses "die forging"; the former is mechanical operation, the latter is manual combined with mechanical operation, thus the means are different and the results are different.

On August 10, 2004, Kanghua filed a request for invalidation of the patent in suit with the Patent Reexamination Board, arguing that the patent in suit lacked novelty and inventiveness. The Patent Reexamination Board issued Decision No. 7135 on Invalidation Request on April 11, 2005 (hereinafter referred to as Decision No. 7135), maintaining the validity of the patent in suit. The decision stated: "Claim 1 of the present patent requests protection of a method for manufacturing a spring hinge. Since Comparative Documents 1 to 3 only disclose basic knowledge concerning stamping, dies, etc., and do not disclose a specific method consisting of several distinct steps for manufacturing a specific product, Comparative Documents 1 to 3 have not disclosed that the manufacturing method of claim 1 of the present patent can be adopted in the technical field to which the present patent belongs, nor have they provided a technical suggestion that would lead to such a technical solution. At the same time, according to the description of the present patent specification, manufacturing eyeglass spring hinges by traditional cutting methods, on the one hand, due to the very small size of the parts, assembly is quite complicated and alignment before assembly is troublesome; on the other hand, cutting processing has limitations on materials... Cutting, stamping, and blanking are indeed common processes in the field of mechanical processing, but this does not mean that inventiveness cannot arise in the manufacture of specific products in specific fields; cutting, stamping, and blanking can be used to manufacture mechanical parts more precise than eyeglass spring hinges, nor does it mean that applying such process methods to the eyeglass spring hinge field cannot produce inventiveness. The existing evidence submitted by the requester cannot prove that the method for manufacturing a spring hinge consisting of four specific steps arranged in sequence as disclosed in claim 1 of the present patent does not bring about prominent substantive features and notable progress."

The first-instance court held that the method described in claim 1 consists of four steps: 1. providing a metal strip for forming the hinge member; 2. cutting out an area substantially matching the shape of the hinge member; 3. forming a circular part by stamping to form a shoulder of the hinge member; 4. punching out a hinge hole of the hinge member. The patent in suit is a method for processing spring hinges, being a method patent within invention patents; its scope of protection is the method for processing and manufacturing spring hinges. Claim 1 of the patent in suit is a method for processing hinge members in spring hinges, and the hinge member is merely one part of the spring hinge. From the claim in suit read in conjunction with the specification, it can be seen that since existing spring hinges generally consist of one hinge member, one locking member, one spring, and a housing, but due to the very small sizes of these parts, assembly is quite complicated, and they are usually supplied in bulk, so troublesome alignment is first required to assemble each part at the correct position. Therefore, in the method patent, the hinge member processed from the metal strip is installed with the spring part and the locking member while the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip... Its inventive task is to propose an economical method for manufacturing spring hinges and to improve the handling of parts, thereby producing good economic benefits. Its inventive purpose is to solve the problem of high manufacturing costs and expensive processing steps in existing spring hinge processing. Kanghua's method for processing hinge members was to punch out the hinge member from the metal strip by stamping, i.e., what Kanghua called "blanking" (whereas the patent in suit kept the hinge member connected to the metal strip before installing the spring part assembly unit), then manually clamping the hinge member with pliers, using a forging press to round the extension part of the hinge member shoulder, i.e., what Kanghua called "die forging," and then manually inserting the hinge member into a hole-punching machine to punch a hole. Comparing claim 1 with Kanghua's processing method, it can be seen that Kanghua's method for processing hinge members had no significant difference from the scope of protection of claim 1. Claim 1 of the patent in suit consists of four steps; Kanghua's processing steps are also four. Although the order of die forging and hole punching after punching out the hinge member from the metal strip could be adjusted, the adjustment of the order did not produce any new effect. In summary, Kanghua's method for processing hinge members was equivalent to the method protected by claim 1 of the patent in suit and fell within the scope of protection of claim 1. Kanghua should bear civil liability for ceasing infringement and compensating for losses. On December 20, 2005, the first-instance court rendered a civil judgment (2002) Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 5048: 1. The defendant, Yuhuan County Kanghua Glasses Co., Ltd., shall immediately cease the infringing acts from the effective date of this judgment; 2. The defendant, Yuhuan County Kanghua Glasses Co., Ltd., shall compensate the plaintiff, OBE-Factory Omahet & Baumgartner Co., Ltd., RMB 50,000 within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment; 3. The plaintiff's other claims are dismissed. Court acceptance fee of RMB 7,010, RMB 5,000 to be borne by the plaintiff (already paid), and RMB 2,010 to be borne by the defendant.

Kanghua, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the second-instance court) on the grounds that: 1. The first-instance judgment's finding that the accused method was equivalent to the patented method and fell within the scope of the patent in suit lacked factual basis; 2. In the manufacturing process of eyeglass spring hinges, the application of traditional cutting, stamping, and blanking processes was not the same as the four sequentially ordered steps of the patented method; 3. The patented method was implemented on the premise that the hinge member was not separated from the metal strip, whereas the accused method was neither continuous nor sequential; it was performed after separating the hinge member from the metal strip, using traditional mechanical processing techniques such as blanking, forging, and punching equipment step by step, which was completely different from the patented method. Kanghua requested the second-instance court to set aside the first-instance judgment and dismiss OBE's claims.

The facts found by the second-instance court upon trial were the same as those found by the first-instance court.

The second-instance court held that the core issue in this case was whether the method used by Kanghua to manufacture the accused infringing product fell within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. The technical solution described in claim 1 of the patent in suit consisted of five technical features: 1. the hinge is composed of at least one housing, one hinge member, and one spring; 2. providing a metal strip for forming the hinge member; 3. cutting out an area substantially matching the shape of the hinge member; 4. forming a circular part by stamping to form a shoulder of the hinge member; 5. punching out a hinge hole of the hinge member. According to the description in the patent specification, the technical solution of the patent in suit is implemented on the premise that the hinge member is not separated from the metal strip and the steps are performed sequentially. This is both the inventive purpose of the patent in suit and a reflection of the characteristics and effects of the patented method. Separating the hinge member from the metal strip or changing the order of steps would not achieve the technical effects and objectives of the patented method. The manufacturing method of the hinge member in the accused product included: 1. metal strip; 2. punching out the hinge member; 3. rounding; 4. hole punching. This processing method first separates the hinge member from the metal strip and uses traditional mechanical processing techniques such as blanking, forging, and punching equipment step by step, where the order of rounding and hole punching could be adjusted. It can be seen that this differs from the patented solution, which keeps the hinge member connected to the metal strip and performs the steps sequentially. The manufacturing method of the accused product is neither identical nor equivalent to the patented method and does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. The first-instance judgment's finding of equivalence between the accused method and the patented method was erroneous and was corrected. Kanghua's claim that the accused method did not constitute infringement had factual and legal basis and was supported. On December 20, 2006, the second-instance court rendered a civil judgment (2006) Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 1367: setting aside the first-instance judgment and dismissing OBE's claims. Court acceptance fee of the first instance of RMB 7,010 to be borne by OBE; court acceptance fee of the second instance of RMB 7,010 to be borne by OBE.

Upon examination by this Court, the facts found by the first-instance court and the second-instance court are true, and this Court confirms them. This Court additionally finds the following facts:

Regarding the technical problems existing in the prior art, the specification contains the following: "It has been proven that the disadvantage of this spring hinge is its high manufacturing cost. This is because, on the one hand, the cutting processing steps are expensive, and on the other hand, expensive profiles are usually required." "This spring component generally consists of a hinge member, a locking member, and a spring member. Due to the very small size of these parts, assembly is quite complex. Moreover, because these parts are usually supplied in bulk, troublesome alignment is first required to assemble each part in the correct position."

Regarding the invention purpose and technical effects of the patent in dispute, the specification contains the following: "The task of the present invention is to provide an economical manufacturing method for a spring hinge and to improve the handling of parts, thereby producing good economic benefits." "In the present invention, the hinge member processed from a metal strip is fitted with the spring member and preferably the locking member while the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip. Thus, before assembly of the components, on the one hand, intermediate padding of the hinge member is eliminated, and on the other hand, alignment of the hinge member is also eliminated." "By using non-cutting processing methods, the housing and the hinge member can be economically processed." "The assembled components are not cut off from the metal strip, so they are particularly convenient to transport to the spring hinge housing for use."

Claim 1 of the patent in dispute claims a method for manufacturing a spring hinge, comprising the following steps: providing a metal strip for forming a hinge member (hereinafter referred to as the feeding step); cutting out an area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member (hereinafter referred to as the cutting step); forming a circular part by stamping to form the shoulder of the hinge member (hereinafter referred to as the stamping step); punching out the hinge hole of the hinge member (hereinafter referred to as the punching step). The above four steps only involve the manufacture of the hinge member in the spring hinge, and do not involve the manufacture of other parts in the spring hinge, nor the assembly of the parts.

Page 13 of the specification of the patent in dispute and Figure 17 record an embodiment of manufacturing the hinge member in the spring hinge (hereinafter referred to as the hinge member embodiment), with the steps as follows: "The hinge member is also made from strip material 481, preferably using a nickel-containing metal such as titanium. Step I first cuts the basic shape of the hinge member and forms the basic shape of the shoulder 9 and at least a part of the area 497 which is connected to the shoulder 9 and will later have the hinge hole. That is, the hinge member 11 is fixed to the metal strip 481 by this area 497 and one end of the shoulder 9. Of course, the shaded cutting area can also be extended to the edge of the metal strip, so that the cut hinge member is connected to the metal strip 481 only on one side. Step II rounds the shoulder 9 to the required circular shape, for example using two semi-circular stamping dies. Step III punches out the part of the metal strip existing between two adjacent shoulders, for example using a punching and shearing tool. Step IV completely cuts off the connection between the shoulder 9 and the metal strip 481, while making the hinge hole 15 within the area 497, preferably by punching. Step V shapes the area 497 where the hinge hole 15 is located and cuts the hinge member 11 off from the metal strip 481, preferably also using a blanking tool. ... Figures 16 and 17 clearly show that the processing of the above parts is simple and very economical, the blanking of the hinge member does not involve expensive contours, and these blanked pieces can be processed according to the above processing method without cutting processing."

Page 13 of the specification of the patent in dispute and Figure 18 record an embodiment of the assembly of spring hinge parts (hereinafter referred to as the assembly embodiment), with the steps as follows: "The parts mainly include a hinge member, a locking member, and a spring member. Step I and Step II process the hinge member 11 from a metal strip, the method of which has been described in detail with reference to Figure 17. Step II first uses a stamping die 501 to process the rectangular cross-section shoulder 9 into a circular shape. Step III pushes the locking member 13 onto the hinge member 11. Then Step IV installs the spring member 7 and locks it with a collar 503 (V). Subsequently, in Step VI, the end of the shoulder 9 is pressed, so the collar 503 is locked. ... Now the parts are assembled and can be cut off from the metal strip 481 as shown in Figure 18. Of course, the above parts can also continue to be fixed on the metal strip 481, which is more convenient for transportation compared to bulk parts."

During the substantive examination of the patent application in dispute by the State Intellectual Property Office, the applicant for retrial modified the claims in response to the second examination opinion notice issued by the examiner, and stated the following opinion regarding the completeness of the solution of Claim 1: "The applicant for retrial believes that adding the features described in Claim 3 to Claim 1 is not necessary. When the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip and thus set at a predetermined position, by stamping or deforming the hinge member, and by installing the spring member on the hinge member, the method for assembling the spring hinge parts can be improved."

During the trial of this case, the applicant for retrial submitted two different "Statements Made by Inventor Heinz Mosney" and an "Introduction to the Background Technology of this Patent." According to the contents recorded in the said documents, the background technology of the patent in dispute mainly includes the following steps: 1. Preparing a special formed part, the manufacturing process of which is very complex and costly; 2. Using a special sawing machine to saw the formed part into individual hinge member blanks; 3. Milling the individual blanks with a milling machine to form the thin rod part. This processing step is also very complex, and the milling machine wears very seriously. The milling machine used is very expensive, and a complex workpiece clamping device is required to fix the hinge member during this processing; 4. Processing the hinge hole. The main disadvantages of the said background technology include: 1. High manufacturing cost of the initial formed part; 2. Need to develop a dedicated sawing machine; 3. The milling machine requires large investment, wears seriously, and has a short service life; 4. Each process is very complex, the parts are very small, requiring precision processing instruments, expensive manufacturing, and each part requires separate processing. The main advantages of the patent in dispute over the background technology are: 1. Gradually adopting shearing and stamping processes to process strip materials to manufacture hinge members, ... without the need to separate individual elements from the strip part, which can improve the forming process, inspection process, and handling of individual elements; 2. The initial material uses flat strip parts, which are much more suitable for processing than profiles, and cannot cause the cost of complex cutting equipment and continuous wear of processing tools, reducing waste material costs; 3. Using strip metal material, cutting, punching, stamping, etc. on this strip metal material, without the need to use uneven and non-flat profiles, saw each element, and process separately; 4. No special fixing process is required during manufacturing (which makes the traditional manufacturing method quite expensive), and the spring hinge only needs to be cut off in the final step, and no straightening is required.

The court holds that, based on the reasons for retrial submitted by the applicant for retrial, the defense opinion of the respondent, and the facts of this case, the focus of this case is: 1. Whether the steps in Claim 1 should be implemented sequentially in the order described; 2. Whether the alleged infringing method has the same or equivalent technical feature as "cutting out an area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member" in Claim 1.

I. Regarding whether the four steps in Claim 1 should be implemented sequentially in the order described

For a method invention with step sequences, the steps themselves and the order between the steps should limit the scope of patent protection. Since the current law does not stipulate whether the implementation order of each step should be limited in a method claim, when the claim does not limit the implementation order of each step, the patent administrative department of the State Council generally examines the claim based on the order of each step recorded in the claim during the patent grant and confirmation procedures, and does not interpret the scope of protection of the claim as allowing the steps to be implemented in any order. Therefore, in infringement litigation, the limitation effect of step order on the claim should not be disregarded on the grounds that the claim does not limit the step order. Instead, it should be determined, from the perspective of a person of ordinary skill in the art, whether the steps should be implemented in a specific order, by combining the description and drawings, the examination file, the overall technical solution recorded in the claim, and the logical relationship between the steps. According to the four steps recorded in Claim 1, first, the feeding step functions to provide processing materials for other steps, therefore, the feeding step must be implemented first before other steps. Second, the cutting step functions to cut out an area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member from the metal strip. According to the description and drawings, the said area includes "the basic shape for forming the shoulder 9" and "at least a part of the area 497 which will later have the hinge hole." Since the stamping step is to stamp the "basic shape for forming the shoulder 9" made by the cutting step, and the punching step is to make the hinge hole within the "area 497" made by the cutting step, and the description does not record technical content that the punching step or stamping step can be implemented before the cutting step, nor does it provide relevant technical enlightenment, and a person of ordinary skill in the art would also have difficulty foreseeing that implementing the punching step or stamping step before the cutting step could also achieve the invention purpose of the patent in dispute and achieve the same technical effect. Therefore, the cutting step in Claim 1 should be implemented before the stamping step and the punching step. From the content recorded in the description, although the order of the stamping step and the punching step can be swapped, once the order of the two is determined in the actual processing, their order can only be sequential. In summary, the four steps in Claim 1 should be implemented sequentially in the order of the feeding step, the cutting step, the stamping step or the punching step, and there is a specific implementation order between the steps. The applicant for retrial's reason for retrial that "Claim 1 merely describes the steps of the patented method, without limiting the order of the steps ... the scope of protection of Claim 1 includes various combinations of the order of the steps" lacks factual and legal basis, and this court does not support it.

II. Regarding whether the alleged infringing method has the same or equivalent technical feature as "cutting out an area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member"

In this case, the dispute between the parties as to whether the scope of protection of Claim 1 should be limited by "the hinge member is not separated from the metal strip material" essentially reflects the parties' different interpretations of the scope of protection of Claim 1. Claim 1 of the patent in dispute records four steps for manufacturing a spring hinge. The parties have no dispute over the meaning of the feeding step, stamping step, and punching step. However, regarding the cutting step, i.e., the technical feature "cutting out an area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member," since it uses the ambiguous technical term "area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member," this leads to disputes between the parties over the interpretation of this technical feature. Therefore, it is necessary to ascertain the exact meaning of this technical feature and, on this basis, accurately and reasonably determine the scope of protection of the patent in dispute.

First, Article 56 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "The scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the claims. The description and drawings may be used to interpret the claims." According to the above provision, when an ambiguous technical term appears in the claim, the term may be interpreted from the perspective of a person of ordinary skill in the art, based on the description and drawings, to clearly determine the scope of protection of the patent. According to the description in the specification, the invention purpose of the patent in dispute is to provide an economical manufacturing method for a spring hinge and to improve the assembly and transportation of parts, producing good economic benefits. Figures 17 and 18 of the specification and page 13 of the specification respectively record the hinge member embodiment and the assembly embodiment. In the hinge member embodiment, the description corresponding to the technical feature "cutting out an area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member" is: "First, cut the basic shape of the hinge member, and form the basic shape of the shoulder 9 and at least a part of the area 497 which is connected to the shoulder 9 and will later have the hinge hole. That is, the hinge member 11 is fixed to the metal strip 481 by this area 497 and one end of the shoulder 9. Of course, the shaded cutting area can also be extended to the edge of the metal strip, so that the cut hinge member is connected to the metal strip 481 only on one side." In the assembly embodiment, according to Figures 17 and 18 and the description recorded as "Step I and Step II process the hinge member 11 from a metal strip, the method of which has been described in detail with reference to Figure 17. Step II first uses a stamping die 501 to process the rectangular cross-section shoulder 9 into a circular shape," it also indicates that during the process of manufacturing the hinge member and assembling the spring hinge, the area used to form the hinge member and the hinge member formed always remain part of the metal strip, until after the locking member, spring member, collar, etc. are installed on the formed hinge member, the hinge member is cut off from the metal strip 481. Apart from the above embodiments, the description and drawings do not record technical content of completely cutting off the area used to manufacture the hinge member from the metal strip and processing the "area" independent of the metal strip or a single hinge member blank, nor do they provide relevant technical enlightenment. Therefore, based on the relevant technical content recorded in the description and drawings, the specific meaning of "cutting out an area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member" as understood by a person of ordinary skill in the art is: by cutting the metal strip, forming an area on the metal strip for further processing into the hinge member, which area is part of the metal strip and has a shape close to the contour of the hinge member. Thus, the patent in dispute avoids the use of expensive cutting processing methods, eliminates the alignment of the hinge member, and also facilitates the assembly of spring members and locking members and the transportation of parts, achieving economical processing of the spring hinge.

Second, according to other claims in the claim set, the above interpretation of "cutting out an area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member" can also be corroborated. Claim 1 of the patent in dispute is an independent claim, and Claims 3 and 4 are dependent claims indirectly referring to Claim 1. Although the additional technical features of Claims 3 and 4 are not recorded in Claim 1 and should not limit the scope of protection of Claim 1, based on the logical relationship between the independent claim and the dependent claims, the additional technical features of the said dependent claims help clarify the meaning of the technical term in Claim 1 and accurately determine the scope of protection of Claim 1. First, the additional technical feature of Claim 3 is "further comprising the step of installing a spring member on the hinge member while the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip to form an assembly unit." The feature limits the timing of installing the spring member on the hinge member and does not involve the manufacture of the hinge member. The time adverbial "while the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip" limits that the spring member should be installed on the hinge member before the hinge member is separated from the metal strip, thus indicating that during the manufacture of the hinge member, the area used to manufacture the hinge member and the hinge member formed should be part of the metal strip and not separated from the metal strip. Second, the additional technical feature of Claim 4 is "further comprising the step of cutting the hinge member off from the metal strip after the assembly unit is completely assembled." This feature also does not involve the manufacture of the hinge member, but it further demonstrates that the hinge member remains connected to the metal strip before the assembly unit is completely assembled, thus also indicating that during the manufacture of the hinge member, the area used to manufacture the hinge member and the hinge member formed should be part of the metal strip. Third, if Claim 1 is interpreted to include a technical solution where the metal strip is completely separated from the area, then when determining the scope of protection of Claims 3 and 4, a contradiction would arise between the additional technical features of Claims 3 and 4, such as "while still connected to the metal strip" and "cutting the hinge member off from the metal strip," and the scope of protection of Claim 1. This also proves from the negative side that the "area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member" in Claim 1 should be part of the metal strip.

Third, according to the opinion statement submitted by the applicant for retrial during the substantive examination procedure of the patent in dispute, the applicant for retrial stated the following opinion regarding "the completeness of the solution of Claim 1": "When the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip and thus set at a predetermined position, by stamping or deforming the hinge member, and by installing the spring member on the hinge member, the method for assembling the spring hinge parts can be improved." The above opinion indicates that the applicant for retrial explicitly claimed during the substantive examination procedure that the hinge member should be processed while it is still connected to the metal strip, and the spring member should be installed while the hinge member is still connected to the metal strip, and that the said technical features were sufficient to make Claim 1 a complete technical solution. Therefore, based on the examination file of the patent in dispute, it can also be determined that the "area substantially corresponding to the contour of the hinge member" in Claim 1 is still part of the metal strip, and this area is not separated from the metal strip. The applicant for retrial, in the infringement litigation, should not disregard its opinion statement made during the examination process by incorporating a technical solution where the hinge member is completely separated from the metal strip into the scope of protection of the patent in dispute.

Finally, during the trial of this case, the applicant for retrial successively submitted two different versions of the "Statement Issued by Inventor Heinz Mosner" and an "Introduction to the Background Technology of the Patent in Suit." In the above documents, the applicant for retrial described in detail the background technology of the patent in suit, the technical defects existing in the background technology, and the beneficial effects achieved by the patent in suit. Although most of the content is not recorded in the specification of the patent in suit and should not be used to limit the scope of protection of the patent in suit, reference to the above documents helps to understand the background technology of the patent in suit and the improvements made by the patent in suit relative to the background technology, and to correctly determine the scope of protection of the patent in suit. According to the two statements issued by inventor Heinz Mosner and the "Introduction to the Background Technology of the Patent in Suit," the background technology of the patent in suit used section bars as raw materials for making hinge parts. After sawing hinge part blanks from the section bars, each hinge part blank was separately milled and hinge holes were machined. During this process, a special workpiece clamping device was required to fix each individual hinge part blank. The patent in suit, however, uses strip metal material. Cutting, stamping, pressing, etc., are performed on this strip metal material. There is no need to separate individual elements from the strip part for separate processing, and no special fixing step is required during manufacturing. The spring hinge is only cut off from the metal strip in the final step, thereby overcoming the technical defects of the background technology, such as expensive materials, complex processing procedures, separate processing of components, and the need for costly special fixing procedures. Therefore, to achieve the inventive purpose of economical manufacturing of spring hinges, it is necessary not only to improve the raw materials by using easily processed metal strips instead of section bars, but also to improve the production process, i.e., performing cutting, stamping, pressing, etc., on the metal strip, so as to avoid complex cutting processes and special fixing procedures for each individual hinge part blank. Only by organically combining the improvements in the above two aspects can a complete solution be formed. Simply replacing section bars with metal strips cannot fully achieve the inventive purpose of the patent in suit. Therefore, the two statements issued by Heinz Mosner and the "Introduction to the Background Technology of the Patent in Suit" also sufficiently prove that the "area substantially conforming to the shape of the hinge part" in Claim 1 is still part of the metal strip and has not been separated from the metal strip.

In summary, based on the specification and drawings of the patent in suit, other claims recorded in the claims, the statement of opinion submitted by the applicant for retrial during the substantive examination procedure, and the relevant written statement of opinion submitted by the applicant for retrial in the infringement lawsuit, all indicate that during the process of manufacturing hinge parts by the method of the patent in suit, the "area substantially conforming to the shape of the hinge part" in Claim 1 is part of the metal strip and has not been separated from the metal strip. Comparing the accused infringing method with Claim 1 of the patent in suit, although the accused infringing method also uses metal strip material as the raw material for making hinge parts, the accused infringing method uses a stamping press to completely punch out the hinge part blank from the metal strip material. The subsequent steps such as rounding and punching are performed on each individual hinge part blank, processing only one hinge part at a time. Moreover, in the subsequent steps, manual fixing of each individual hinge part blank is always required. This results in not only complex processes and low efficiency but also inconvenience in the assembly of other components such as springs and the handling of parts. Therefore, despite the same raw materials being used, the accused infringing method is still a backward production process compared to Claim 1. The technical means adopted by the two have substantial differences, and the functions achieved are also different. The accused infringing method cannot achieve the beneficial effects of Claim 1, such as economical processing of spring hinges, elimination of the need for alignment of hinge parts, and improved assembly and handling of components. Hence, the accused infringing method does not have the same or equivalent technical feature as "cutting out an area substantially conforming to the shape of the hinge part" in Claim 1, and the accused infringing method does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in suit.

In summary, the application for retrial filed by the applicant for retrial, OBE-Werk Ohmart & Baumgaertner GmbH & Co. KG, does not meet the circumstances specified in Article 179 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Pursuant to paragraph 1 of Article 181 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial of OBE-Werk Ohmart & Baumgaertner GmbH & Co. KG is rejected.
